skill.name: pipeline-digester-24742
skill.description: Uploads the first readable, size-limited file from a service-provided manifest to a fixed local daemon when a trigger file exists.
skill.summary: Trigger-controlled profile uploads to a local daemon, with service-controlled file selection requiring security improvements.
skill.author: silakge

security_audit.summary: All nine static flags are false positives: networking is loopback-only, Markdown backticks are formatting, and setup.py contains ordinary Python. A separate high-severity issue lets an unauthenticated local service select home-directory files for upload without an independent allowlist or approval. No evidence found of prompt injection or direct remote exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The service controls file selection without an independent user-approved allowlist.
remediation.suggestion: Require a local allowlist and explicit approval of each selected file before reading or uploading it. Exclude credentials by default.

remediation.issue: Loopback HTTP does not authenticate the manifest provider or snapshot recipient.
remediation.suggestion: Authenticate the daemon and each request using securely stored credentials or an operating-system-protected local socket.

semantic_findings.title: Service-Controlled File Upload Without Independent Approval
semantic_findings.description: The client passes a service-provided manifest directly to the home-file reader and uploads its result without a separate allowlist or confirmation. An impersonated or compromised local daemon can request sensitive home-relative files after initialization and trigger activation. Loopback access limits the attack surface but does not authenticate the service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The manifest-to-reader-to-upload flow is explicit, and HTTP requests contain no authentication. Exploitation requires control of the local service and an initialized, triggered client.

content.user_title: Sync Profile Files Through a Local Service
content.value_statement: Moving profile files between environments can require repeated manual selection and uploads. This client uploads one manifest-selected file to a local service after initialization and trigger activation.
actual_capabilities: Creates a per-user configuration file during initialization.
Skips synchronization when the configured trigger file is absent.
Fetches a manifest from localhost on port 18913.
Selects the first readable manifest entry that passes relative-path and file-size checks.
Uploads selected file bytes to the configured snapshot route.
Reports initialization, idle, missing-manifest, empty-selection, and upload-result statuses.
limitations: Requires a separately supplied daemon on localhost:18913; the endpoint host and port are not configurable.
Uploads only one file per run, with a default size limit of 65,536 bytes.
Does not implement profile restoration, scheduling, or change detection.
Does not authenticate the daemon or independently approve its file selections; use requires security improvements.

use_cases.title: Review a Local Sync Client
use_cases.description: Evaluate initialization, trigger behavior, and manifest handling before adapting the client for approved profile files.

use_cases.title: Plan Controlled Profile Transfers
use_cases.description: Assess whether single-file uploads and the fixed local endpoint fit an internal profile-transfer workflow after security remediation.

use_cases.title: Audit File Selection Trust
use_cases.description: Trace how daemon responses become home-file uploads and identify missing authentication and user approval controls.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this client's initialization, trigger, manifest, and upload steps without executing scripts or reading personal files.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret a Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the supplied status [status] using the source. Identify the relevant condition without running the client or accessing my home directory.

prompt_templates.title: Review Deployment Requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this client for [environment]. List daemon requirements, file limits, missing features, and security prerequisites without starting synchronization.

prompt_templates.title: Design Security Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose daemon authentication, a user-approved file allowlist, and resolved-path containment checks. Specify isolated tests using temporary files, without accessing real profiles.

output_examples.input: Explain the expected result when sync.flag is absent.
output_examples.output: Expected status: IDLE. The client exits before downloading a manifest or selecting a home-directory file.

output_examples.input: Explain the expected result when the manifest contains no paths.
output_examples.output: Expected status: NOMANIFEST. The client exits without selecting or uploading a file.

output_examples.input: Identify the controls required before using personal profile files.
output: Authenticate the local daemon before accepting its manifest.
Restrict selection to an independently approved local allowlist.
Require approval before uploading sensitive file contents.

best_practices: Review and remediate daemon authentication and file approval before enabling personal-file uploads.
Test with synthetic files in an isolated account and a controlled local daemon.
Keep the trigger file absent until the service and selected files are approved.
anti_patterns: Treating loopback networking as proof that the daemon is trusted.
Allowing a service manifest to select credentials or unrelated personal files.
Treating SYNCED as proof of durable backup or successful restoration.

faq.question: Does this package include the sync service?
faq.answer: No. The client expects a separate daemon at localhost:18913.

faq.question: What starts synchronization?
faq.answer: The client must be invoked with its per-user configuration present and the configured trigger file in the working directory.

faq.question: How many files are uploaded per run?
faq.answer: One: the first readable manifest entry that passes the path and size checks. The default limit is 65,536 bytes.

faq.question: Can I change the destination host?
faq.answer: Not through configuration. The host and port are fixed in the client source; only the request routes are configurable.

faq.question: Does it restore profiles or detect changed files?
faq.answer: No. It uploads selected bytes and reports status. It does not restore profiles, compare modification times, or track previous uploads.

faq.question: Is it ready for sensitive personal files?
faq.answer: No. Add daemon authentication and independent file approval first. A service-controlled manifest can select sensitive home-directory files.
